question.text: Which one of the following cannot be prepared from <math> <mrow> <msub> <mtext>B</mtext> <mtext>2</mtext> </msub> <msub> <mtext>H</mtext> <mtext>6</mtext> </msub> <mtext>?</mtext></mrow> </math>

solution.text: In diborane, <math> <mrow>  <msub>   <mrow>    <mtext>(B</mtext></mrow>   <mtext>2</mtext>  </msub>  <msub>   <mtext>H</mtext>   <mtext>6</mtext>  </msub>  <mtext>)</mtext></mrow></math> molecule, only four terminal hydrogen atoms are replaceable. The two bridge <math> <mtext>H</mtext></math>-atoms cannot be substituted. Hence <math> <mrow>  <msub>   <mtext>B</mtext>   <mtext>2</mtext>  </msub>  <msub>   <mrow>    <msub>     <mrow>      <mtext>(CH</mtext></mrow>     <mtext>3</mtext>    </msub>    <mtext>)</mtext></mrow>   <mtext>6</mtext>  </msub>  </mrow></math> cannot be prepared from <math> <mrow>  <msub>   <mtext>B</mtext>   <mtext>2</mtext>  </msub>  <msub>   <mtext>H</mtext>   <mtext>6</mtext>  </msub>  <mo>.</mo></mrow></math>
